text:
support-ops: FYI -- multiple customers reporting 500s from the hosted API on /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. They expect 429s for quota hits. Escalating.
alex.k: seeing a spike in 500s in errors.dashboard for the edge gateway. first seen at 09:10, matches support reports. sample req id: rq_0a1b2c3d
maya.s: can you paste a curl repro if you have one? or at least the X-Request-Id so we can trace
support-ops: here's one from customer A: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_0a1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}'

-> 500 response body: {"error":"internal_server_error","message":"admission failure"}

jordan_oncall: checking envoy logs at the edge... seeing 502s thrown by admission-control upstream. envoy shows upstream_timeout for 10-15% of requests in that window
sam_db: admissions svc recently rolled ~03:00 UTC today (maya's team). any config changes?
maya.s: yes rolled a small change to admission-control to call the new enforcement-cache before fallback to rlimit. change was to short-circuit for cold starts. didn't expect errors.
alex.k: getting a trace from the gateway for rq_0a1b2c3d -> admission-control -> enforcement-cache (cache call) -> rlimit-service. enforcement-cache timed out (504) and admission-control returned 500 instead of mapping to 429. stack excerpt:

```
Error: enforcement-cache timeout
  at EnforcementClient.call (/srv/admission/index.js:142)
  at processRequest (/srv/admission/handler.js:88)
  at Object.<anonymous> (/srv/admission/server.js:45)
  at step (/usr/src/node_modules/async/series.js:12)
```

jordan_oncall: looks like admission-control treats dependency timeouts as fatal and returns 500. we should map dependency timeout -> quota-check-unavailable -> fall back to permissive quota or return 429 when enforcement says over limit. For now customers see 500.
infra-bot: kubectl get pods -n prod admission-control => 5/5 ready, restart count low. no obvious pod crash
support-ops: list of impacted customers so far: cust_alpha, cust_bravo, cust_charlie (some with high QPS). severity customer escalations incoming.
maya.s: rolling back the enforcement-cache change now to see if error rate drops. initiating rollback canary to 10% at 09:30UTC. @deploy-bot please run.
deploy-bot: rollback started, canary 10% -> 0% at 09:31 UTC. status: in progress
alex.k: added a short query to logs: filter admission-control errors where upstream==enforcement-cache and code==504, count ~420 in last 15m
jordan_oncall: also seeing a correlation with increased latencies from enforcement-cache cluster in us-west-2. maybe transient DB pool exhaustion? sam any DB metrics?
sam_db: DB pool metrics spiking for enforcement-cache connections 09:05-09:20. there was a misconfigured retry loop in enforcement-cache that caused connection pile-up after a downstream slow query. pushing a hotfix to reduce retries at 09:34
maya.s: rollback complete at 09:33 UTC, error rate dropped ~60% immediately but still some residual 500s
alex.k: after rollback, majority of 500s map to admission-control handling of enforcement-cache timeouts. need short-term mitigation: admission-control should translate enforcement-cache timeout -> treat as "quota check unavailable" and do graceful fallback: 1) for requests with prior usage < threshold, allow, 2) for high-QPS customers return 429 instead of 500.
jordan_oncall: implementing a runtime toggle now: ADMISSION_FALLBACK_PERMISSIVE=true for low-tier traffic. patching and deploying to canary at 09:40
deploy-bot: patch deploy to admission-control canary done 09:42, health ok
support-ops: customer messages: cust_bravo confirms retries now return 429 and backoff better. cust_alpha still seeing intermittent 500s (low volume)
alex.k: added alert rule to map admission-control.dependency_timeout -> pager if rate > 50/min and fraction of 500s > 5% so we don't miss mapping issues next time
maya.s: root cause summary draft: enforcement-cache had a retry loop regression causing DB connection storm -> enforcement-cache timeouts -> admission-control treated dependency timeouts as 500s (internal error) instead of mapping to quota/429 or permissive fallback. Deploy change earlier introduced new call path (enforcement-cache) without hardened timeout translations.
sam_db: action items: revert retry change in enforcement-cache repo, add DB-side circuit-breaker + pooled connections guard, add latency SLO on enforcement-cache
jordan_oncall: ops actions: admission-control must map dependency 504/timeout -> 429 or fallback permissive per policy. add integration test to ensure 504 from enforcement-cache doesn't surface as 500 to caller
support-ops: mitigation already: rollback + permissive canary. customers mostly recovered. still watching for stragglers. notifying impacted customers with explanation + compensation offers.
maya.s: I'll own follow-up postmortem and timeline. planning a patch to admission-control to explicitly map dependency errors to 429 with config-driven policy. target PR by EOD.
alex.k: adding a checklist for next 24h: 1) permanent fix merged, 2) enforcement-cache retry revert + limits, 3) run chaos test that injects enforcement-cache 504s and ensure callers return 429 or permissive allow, 4) update runbook to include mapping rules. 
support-ops: marking this thread for postmortem and customer comms. thanks all. :thumbsup:
